name: Digital Infrastructure
one_liner: Owners of towers, fiber networks, and data centers that lease shared capacity on long-term contracts, a real-estate-like business defined by high upfront cost and high operating leverage.
how_it_makes_money: Tower companies lease antenna space to carriers on long contracts with built-in escalators, earning more as additional tenants are added to each site. Fiber providers sell wholesale and enterprise connectivity, and data-center operators lease space, power, and interconnection to cloud, AI, and enterprise customers.
revenue_formula: Tower revenue = sites × tenants per site × rent per tenant (with annual escalators)
Data center revenue = leased power capacity (MW) × price per kW per month
Fiber revenue = route miles × lit services sold × price per service
cost_structure: Capex: construction of towers, fiber routes, and data-center shells and electrical systems
Power: the largest operating cost for data centers, often passed through to tenants
Ground leases and land: rents paid to landowners under towers
Interest expense: heavy debt financing, since assets are long-lived and stable
margins: Mature tower businesses earn very high EBITDA margins, often around 60%+, because adding a tenant to an existing site costs little. Data centers run lower, roughly 40-50%, with tenancy, power costs, and leverage driving the spread.

key_metrics.name: Tenancy ratio
key_metrics.what: Average tenants per tower; each extra tenant adds high-margin revenue.

key_metrics.name: Adjusted funds from operations (AFFO)
key_metrics.what: Cash earnings measure used to value infrastructure REITs and dividend capacity.

key_metrics.name: Power capacity (MW)
key_metrics.what: Critical load a data center can support; the unit in which capacity is sold.

key_metrics.name: Occupancy / utilization
key_metrics.what: Share of available space or power leased; drives returns on fixed assets.

key_metrics.name: Churn
key_metrics.what: Lease revenue lost from tenant cancellations, such as carrier consolidation.

key_metrics.name: Yield on cost
key_metrics.what: Annual cash return on the construction cost of a new asset; the key development hurdle.

trends: AI-driven boom in large data-center campuses, with power availability as the binding constraint
Data-center developers pursuing on-site generation, nuclear, and long-term power contracts
Carrier consolidation and slower 5G spending weighing on tower leasing growth
Private equity and infrastructure funds acquiring towers, fiber, and data centers for stable cash yields
Higher interest rates raising financing costs and pressuring valuations
Government funding for rural broadband expanding fiber construction
